findings.statement: CXCL8 is up in all eight cohorts (meta log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.687]) and ranks third in convergence. It is the ligand of the neutrophil circuit, neutrophil CXCL8 to CXCR2 and ACKR1 (see the CXCR2 and ACKR1 findings). This is co-expression, not proof of signalling.

In the Gubatan single-cell data, the CXCL8 to ACKR1 link from neutrophil states (generic Neutrophil, CXCR4, OSM, MX1, PADI4) to ACKR1 endothelium has some of the highest scores seen, and the generic Neutrophil sender rose in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa. This is co-expression only, and ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor that presents chemokines and does not signal conventionally.

Cell source of CXCL8 depends on the atlas. Without neutrophils (Smillie), macrophages and other myeloid cells make most CXCL8 and the myeloid lineage replicates in all three other atlases. When neutrophils are included (Gubatan), neutrophils make most of the CXCL8 transcripts, so the signal in bulk biopsies is largely infiltrating immune cells and not a change of the epithelium or stroma.

CXCR2 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking, with up-regulation in all eight cohorts for CXCR2 and Open Targets genetic support. Its antagonists reached clinical trials: reparixin (phase 3) and ladarixin and SX-682 (phase 2) outside UC, and in UC navarixin and SB-656933, which went no further than phase 2. Its transcripts sit in neutrophils in the single-cell data, and CXCR2 is not replicated as a stromal or T/NK gene across atlases, so it is a neutrophil-recruitment target and not a tissue-intrinsic one.

CXCR2 receivers are neutrophil states. The CXCL8 to CXCR2 link from Neutrophil CXCR4 to the generic Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed versus uninflamed mucosa, consistent with a feed-forward neutrophil recruitment loop. This is co-expression only.

Inflammatory fibroblasts are a stromal sender of CXCL1 to CXCR2 on neutrophils, and the link to the generic Neutrophil state rose strongly in inflamed mucosa. Absolute scores are far lower than the neutrophil CXCL8 circuit. No CXCL1 or CXCL5 drug is listed.

The expected neutrophil OSM to inflammatory fibroblast circuit is weak in this dataset. OSM to IL6ST from Neutrophil OSM to LP fibroblast has a low score and fell versus uninflamed mucosa. Only the Neutrophil PADI4 sender is new in inflamed tissue, with a small score. No inflammatory-fibroblast receiver appeared among the top pairs, so this circuit is not supported here.

IL1B is up in all eight cohorts and has drugs in Open Targets (canakinumab approved, for other diseases). In single-cell data its strongest links go to IL1R2, a decoy receptor, on neutrophil states, sent by monocyte-derived macrophages and neutrophils. So high co-expression does not by itself imply productive IL-1 signalling.

NFkB and TNFa pathway activity are up in all eight cohorts, with the strongest t in the NFkB pathway reaching [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=18.79] in GSE206285. Such broad pathways are poor at discriminating specific circuits.

JAK-STAT, TGFb, EGFR, MAPK, PI3K and Hypoxia pathways are up in all eight cohorts, and WNT in seven of eight (not in GSE73661). Inflamed mucosa activates many pathways at once, so concordance alone is not specific.

STAT3 regulon activity is up in all eight cohorts (t in GSE193677 [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE193677.t=20.6]), and AP1 is also up in all eight cohorts. TF activity is inferred from target genes, not from the TF mRNA.

Not all pathways replicate. VEGF is up in only four cohorts, and Androgen is down in four and up in one, so neither is a consistent signature. These weaker pathways should not be prioritized over the pathways that rise in every cohort.

TREM1 is up in all eight cohorts and has a phase 2 drug (nangibotide), but it returned no ligand-receptor pair above expression thresholds in the single-cell data, so no sender or receiver circuit can be named for it.
AQP9 is up in all eight cohorts, but it has no drug and no genetic support in this ranking, so it is an undrugged, biomarker-like candidate and not a validated target.

caveats: Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression (ligand times receptor mean CP10K) in one single-cell dataset, not signalling.
Pathway and TF activities are inferred by decoupler from bulk mucosal transcriptomes, so they largely reflect immune infiltration and cannot separate tissue-intrinsic change from cell composition.
Many top-ranked genes (CXCL8, CXCL1, S100A8/9, MMPs, AQP9) are neutrophil or myeloid markers, so their ranking may track neutrophil abundance in inflamed biopsies.
IL-23 and integrin axes were not queried in detail; anti-TNF, JAK inhibitor and integrin drug status is not supported by cited records here.
Only top communication rows per gene were read.
